title: Eval & Observability in Spring
objective: After this lesson you will be able to build gold conversation evals with per-component attribution, instrument with SimpleLoggerAdvisor + Micrometer observations, and keep PII out of logs and eval sets alike.
why: 'Works in the demo controller' is not production evidence: advisor chains, tool loops, and RAG retrieval interact in ways unit tests miss. Gold evals with attribution plus observation-backed traces (tokens, latency, verdicts per span) make Spring AI services measurable — and PII discipline keeps measurement legal.

blocks.text: Gold conversations assert per-component expectations: memory resolved the follow-up (advisor), retrieval hit policy chunks (RAG), refund gated (tools), draft met contract (entity). Failures attribute to advisor/tool/prompt respectively — the LangGraph Ch.9 and CrewAI Ch.8 discipline, Spring-flavored. Same-set version diffs gate merges; Testcontainers run RAG/tool integration gold against real pgvector.

blocks.caption: Eval as pipeline: gold → traces → attribution → diffs → gates

blocks.text: Observations: Micrometer spans with AI attributes

Spring AI emits **Micrometer observations** for model and vector-store calls: trace IDs propagate, token/latency attributes attach, dashboards aggregate per operation. Pair with SimpleLoggerAdvisor (DEBUG, PII-scrubbed mappers) for prompt-level detail. Observations answer 'how slow/expensive?' per span; gold answers 'how correct?' per release — operations needs both, neither substitutes.
PII discipline across eval and logs

Gold sets and logs both attract real ticket text — with emails, cards, order IDs. Scrub identically in both (same redaction functions, shared library): eval sets committed scrubbed, logs mapped through redaction pre-persistence. Unscrubbed fixtures violate retention the moment they're committed; unscrubbed logs, the moment they're written.

blocks.title: Attribute the drop
blocks.note: Run it: expect pass with [] then fail naming retrieval — attribution to the component, not the team. Fix location decided by the issue string before any code changes.

items: Gold with per-component slots (memory/retrieval/gate/contract) + forbiddens across happy/edge/attack
Micrometer observations (tokens/latency per span) + scrubbed logger advisors: operations needs both
PII scrubbed identically in eval sets and logs — shared redaction library, committed clean

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice checker on both traces and map verdicts. (b) Add a forbidden-triggering trace (ungated-refund present) and confirm the forbid fires. (c) Write the Testcontainers scope for RAG+tools integration gold (what runs real, what stubs, what asserts).
hints: Verdicts: pass [] / fail [retrieval] — owner named, fix located upstream of generation.
Forbid proof: inject 'ungated-refund' into any field → forbidden fires alongside/ instead of slot issues.
Scope: real pgvector + real tools against seeded fixtures; stubbed model responses (recorded); asserts on retrieval hits + gate holds + contract shapes.
exercise.why: Attribution precision (component owners), invariant guards (forbiddens), and integration scope (real stores, stubbed models) are the three eval judgments — each decisive for different failure classes.
exercise.code: // Eval-scope pattern: real stateful deps, stubbed models, asserted contracts.

quiz.q: All unit tests pass; follow-ups fail in staging. Missing layer?
options: Conversation gold with per-component attribution: memory-resolution failures exist only end to end
quiz.explain: Composition truth (advisor interaction across turns) escapes unit tests structurally. Gold conversations with slots catch integration reality.

quiz.q: Gold set committed with live customer emails. Issue + fix?
options: Retention violation: scrub with the shared redaction library, identical to log scrubbing — committed PII is a breach surface
quiz.explain: Fixtures are code: committed PII violates retention from commit time. Shared scrubbers keep eval and logs equally clean.

quiz.q: Latency regressed; which spans + what attribution?
options: Micrometer per-operation spans: compare p95 per span vs baseline — regressed span names the component (retrieval? tools? model?)
quiz.explain: Observations attribute latency per operation: measurements name components, baselines prove regressions. Instrumented spans replace speculation.

summary: Component-slotted gold, Micrometer + scrubbed logging, PII discipline everywhere, Testcontainers integration scope. Measured Spring services, legally held.
